<reason>PRO better fits the motion's explicit tradeoff: it compared funded, compensated displacement risk under by-right rules against uncompensated displacement from scarcity, while CON's targeted alternative never fully explained how discretionary steering would supply enough homes or stop rent-driven expulsion. CON landed strong points on interim housing and pre-permit buyouts, but PRO's comparative frame remained live.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: extra density cross-subsidizes replacements, predictability lowers costs, and a teardown mandate is an option not an order—so unprofitable teardowns stay standing while housing proceeds on parking lots and commercial sites, flipping CON's fatal-bind argument.</best_rebuttal>
